Both traces solve the problem correctly with identical calculations and final answers. They diverge significantly in verbosity and verification behavior. Trace 1 is highly repetitive, re-executing the same arithmetic calculations (sales, payouts, net change, total) four to five times throughout the trace, adding no new information. Trace 1 also opens several short branches exploring alternative interpretations of "expected cash" (e.g., whether it refers to the drop slip or the total cash), which are quickly discarded for contradicting the prompt's constraints. Trace 2, by contrast, performs each calculation once and proceeds directly to the conclusion without the redundant rework or interpretive side-branches, demonstrating that those divergences in Trace 1 were unnecessary.
